title: Prompts
summary: Prompts are reusable message templates a server offers. A user picks one, often as a slash command, fills its arguments, and the server returns ready-made messages.
useIf: You want a person to start a standard workflow with one action and consistent wording across a team.
avoidIf: Nobody is present to pick it, such as an unattended agent, or the model should choose the workflow itself.

explain.md: Prompts are **user-controlled**. The spec means the user decides when to use one, not who wrote it: the content is defined by the server. A typical host shows prompts as slash commands or menu entries [[tr2]].

A server that supports prompts declares the `prompts` capability, with optional `listChanged`. The client calls `prompts/list` to get `name`, `title`, `description`, `icons` and an optional list of `arguments` (each with `name`, `description` and `required`). It then calls `prompts/get` with the chosen `name` and `arguments`. The result holds `messages`, each with a `role` of `user` or `assistant` and `content` such as text, an image or an embedded resource.

explain.title: A prompt from pick to context

steps.title: List
steps.md: `prompts/list` returns names and arguments. Results carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` in 2026-07-28.

steps.title: Complete
steps.md: `completion/complete` can suggest argument values, up to 100 items [[tr9]].

steps.title: Get
steps.md: `prompts/get` returns messages. The server MAY answer with `input_required` first.

steps.title: Send
steps.md: The host adds the messages to the conversation for the model.

explain.title: Server text is still untrusted text
explain.md: A user selecting a prompt does not make its content safe. The server wrote the messages, and they enter the model's context. Show the expanded text where possible and treat third-party prompt content like any other prompt injection channel.

Lists MAY vary by the authorization on the request, for example to hide prompts a caller's scopes do not allow, but MUST NOT vary per connection. A related extension, Skills over MCP (`io.modelcontextprotocol/skills`), serves `SKILL.md` directories as resources. Host support is still being implemented, so check your host before relying on it [[r11]].

whereToUse: Guided onboarding flows where the first message needs structured arguments
Domain templates that embed a resource, such as a style guide plus the document to review
Standard analyst workflows that must read the same way for every user

use: The wording should be consistent across users
Arguments are few and can be autocompleted
The server owner should maintain the template
avoid: The model must pick the workflow without a user
The workflow needs secrets typed into arguments
The host has no surface to list or pick prompts
flips: A workflow should run unattended: make it a tool or a host-side automation
Teams want to edit templates themselves: keep them in the host or a repository

pitfalls.symptom: Nobody uses the prompts the team shipped
pitfalls.cause: The chosen host does not expose prompts in its UI
pitfalls.fix: Check host support before investing, and offer the same flow as a tool if the host lacks a surface

pitfalls.symptom: Odd behaviour after selecting a third-party prompt
pitfalls.fix: Preview expanded messages, allow-list servers and apply injection defences

scenarios.title: A shared incident summary command
scenarios.situation: On-call engineers across three teams need the same incident summary structure. Each fills in an incident id and severity. A person always starts it.
unknowns: Do all hosts show MCP prompts?
scenarios.question: How do you package the workflow?

options.name: An MCP prompt with two arguments and completion
options.why: User-controlled by design, shared across hosts and consistent for every engineer.
options.tradeoff: Hosts without a prompt surface will not show it.

options.name: A tool the model may call whenever it thinks it is useful
options.why: Works in any host and lets the agent start the summary itself.
options.tradeoff: Less predictable, and the definition costs tokens on every request.

options.name: A wiki page people copy and paste
options.why: Copies drift and arguments are untracked.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable for a one-off before any server exists.

flips.if: The summary must be produced automatically on every alert
flips.then: Use a tool or an automation, since no user is present to pick a prompt.
A host-side saved prompt is simpler.

scenarios.title: Automatic triage on alerts
scenarios.situation: An alert arrives at night and an agent must run a standard triage with no person present. The team wrote the triage as a prompt template.
constraints: Server owned by the SRE team
unknowns: Does the agent framework call tools or only render prompts?
What approvals apply to remediation steps?
scenarios.question: What should the triage flow use?

options.name: A workflow tool the agent or automation calls
options.why: A tool needs no user selection and can return structured findings.
options.tradeoff: Adds a definition and needs approval design for risky actions.

options.name: Keep it as a prompt and have the automation call `prompts/get`
options.why: The automation can fetch the messages and feed the model.
options.tradeoff: You use the prompt primitive outside its user-controlled intent.

options.name: Wait for an engineer to select the prompt
options.tradeoff: Right only when a human should always start triage.

flips.if: A reviewer must approve wording before the run
flips.then: Keep the prompt and require a human to pick it.

flips.if: The triage is only ever started by an on-call engineer
flips.then: A prompt is the better fit again.

scenarios.takeaway: If nobody is there to choose, it is not a prompt.

quiz.q: Which statements about MCP prompts are true?
options: Arguments can be auto-completed with the completion API
Because a user picked it, the content is safe to trust
Returned messages carry a role of `user` or `assistant`
quiz.explain: Prompts are chosen by users, can use `completion/complete` for arguments and return role-tagged messages. The content is still written by the server, so picking it does not make it trustworthy.

quiz.q: A nightly agent must run a standard analysis with nobody present. Which primitive fits?
options: A prompt, since the template is already written
A resource, since it holds the template
A tool or automation that runs without selection
Elicitation, to ask the user which template to use
quiz.explain: Prompts rely on a user choosing them. An unattended run needs a tool or an automation. A resource is attached context and elicitation needs a person to answer.

flashcards.front: Who controls MCP prompts and who writes them?
flashcards.back: The user decides when to use one. The server defines the content, so it is still untrusted text for the model.

flashcards.front: Which calls make up the prompt flow?
flashcards.back: `prompts/list` for names and arguments, optional `completion/complete` for values, then `prompts/get` which returns role-tagged messages.

flashcards.front: When is a prompt the wrong primitive?
flashcards.back: When no human is present to select it or the model should pick the workflow. Use a tool or automation instead.
